body:
This PR introduces a generic framework for driving single-column simulations from netCDF forcing datasets.

Key changes:
- Added ColumnDatasets, a shared interface for reading column forcing files:
	- One native, self-describing format using (z, time) atmospheric variables and (time,) surface variables. It is currently named ClimaColumn, though we can bikeshed on the name.
	- New formats plug in as small dataset modules, with no changes to the forcing, setup, or config code.
- Changed generated ERA5 files to the native column schema. Stale or non-conforming cached files are regenerated from the source rather than read.
- Composed external forcing from per-process terms (HorizontalAdvection, VerticalFluctuation, Nudging, Subsidence) assembled into ExternalDrivenTVForcing, letting runscripts select terms and set per-variable nudging timescales and height masks.
- Added the ColumnFromFile setup, which can source initial conditions, external forcing, surface data, and insolation from one file.
- Extracted shared forcing-tendency kernels, de-duplicating the energy-conversion, nudging, and subsidence math across the GCM, ISDAC, and file-driven paths.
- Renamed the old large-scale-subsidence forcing to LargeScaleSubsidence, freeing the name Subsidence for the new per-process forcing term.
- Ported the ARM VARANAL case onto the interface: a converter (VaranalFiles.to_climacolumn) rewrites pressure-level profile into the native schema, and the case runs through ColumnFromFile. Removed the custom setup and forcing.

Future work (TBD):
- Migrate the cfsite (GCM-driven) case onto the new interface
- Add MOSAiC case?
- Generic in-memory reader, so a runscript can drive forcing from arrays or a non-native format without first writing a native file to disk via to_climacolumn
- Formalize derived variables (quantities computed from the file, e.g. density or vertical velocity) as a first-class part of the interface
- Give the file-driven terms an analytic-target data source, so idealized profiles flow through the same AbstractForcingTerm composition

Documentation to understand the new interface:
- docs/src/single_column_prospect.md section "Column forcing datasets"
- docs/src/setups.md section "Defining a Case in a Runscript"
- Docstrings: `ColumnDatasets`, `AbstractForcingTerm`, `ExternalDrivenTVForcing`, `ColumnFromFile`, `FileHeatFluxes`
title: SCM setup consolidation: ColumnDatasets interface and per-term forcing

body:
To compare with what we had a week ago:

Old sedimentation term:

```
    @. vtt = ifelse(
        ∂a∂z < 0,
        -(ᶜprecipdivᵥ(ᶠρ * Geometry.WVector(ᶠwaχ))),
        -(ᶜa * ᶜprecipdivᵥ(ᶠρ * Geometry.WVector(ᶠwχ))),
    )
```

new sedimentation term:

```
    @. vtt = ifelse(
        ∂a∂z < 0,
        -(ᶜprecipdivᵥ(ᶠρ * Geometry.WVector(ᶠwaχ)) - α_lat * ∂a∂z * ᶜρ⁰w⁰χ⁰),
        -(ᶜa * ᶜprecipdivᵥ(ᶠρ * Geometry.WVector(ᶠwχ))),
    )
```

Old Jacobian term:

```
@. ᶜtridiagonal_matrix_scalar = dtγ * ifelse(ᶜ∂a∂z < 0,
     -(ᶜprecipdivᵥ_matrix()) ⋅ ᶠsed_tracer_advection * DiagonalMatrixRow(ᶜa),
      -DiagonalMatrixRow(ᶜa) ⋅ ᶜprecipdivᵥ_matrix() ⋅ ᶠsed_tracer_advection,
 )
```

new Jacobian term:

```
@. ᶜtridiagonal_matrix_scalar = dtγ * ifelse(ᶜ∂a∂z < 0,
    -(ᶜprecipdivᵥ_matrix()) ⋅ ᶠsed_tracer_advection * DiagonalMatrixRow(ᶜa) +
        DiagonalMatrixRow(α_lat * ᶜ∂a∂z * ᶜρʲs.:(1) * ᶜwʲ / max(1 - ᶜa, eps(eltype(ᶜa)))),
    -DiagonalMatrixRow(ᶜa) ⋅ ᶜprecipdivᵥ_matrix() ⋅ ᶠsed_tracer_advection,
)
````

And I'm setting `α_lat = 0` for now for testing and to recover nightly amip

## Purpose 
<!--- One sentence to describe the purpose of this PR, refer to any linked issues:
#14 -- this will link to issue 14
Closes #2 -- this will automatically close issue 2 on PR merge
-->
Currently, precipitation (rain and snow) is included in the radiation scheme. However, RRTMGP assumes a single effective radius for all liquid water and a single effective radius for all ice. Applying the cloud droplet effective radius to rain is unphysical, as raindrops are significantly larger than cloud droplets. Because rain cannot be represented accurately, we have excluded it, and for consistency, we have excluded snow from the radiative calculations as well. We can come back to it if we can treat cloud condensate and precipitation differently in RRTMGP in the future.

Note: `clwvi` and `clivi` diagnostics are not changed. This may not be consistent with the CMIP convention "only including precipitating hydrometeors when they are included in radiation". I didn't change it because otherwise `clivi` is just a duplicate of `iwp`. We can change it in the future if it's important.
